newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close weaker on CPI data, softer U.S..
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close weaker on CPI data, softer U.S..

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in quiet trade on Wednesday, with prices pulled lower by a decline in U.S. Treasuries and stronger-than-expected Canadian inflation data, analysts said.

"We're down pretty much in step with the U.S. at the longer end," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with financial analysis firm I.D.E.A. "The short end I think is a little bit weighed with the Canadian CPI data."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.55 to C$108.55 to yield 7.267 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond fell 15/32 to yield 6.70 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 57 basis points from 61 basis points at Tuesday's close.

Statistics Canada this morning reported that Canada's November consumer price index rose a higher-than-expected 2.0 percent year-over-year amid higher energy and insurance prices. So-called core inflation, which excludes food and energy costs, rose to 1.4 percent year-over-year, in line with expectations.
The report had a greater impact on the short end of the yield curve as it further reduces expectations of a Bank of Canada rate cut, Kalirai said.
Canadian bonds were also pulled lower by a drop in U.S. Treasury prices, which weakened following an auction of US$18.25 billion in two-year notes.

In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.47 to C$102.53 to 6.648 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 10/32 to yield 6.46 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to 19 basis points from 20 basis points at Tuesday's close.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.96 percent against the U.S. bill at 5.02 percent.
